title: NRF Survey: 142 Million Shoppers Expected for Super Saturday

facts.fact: Nearly 142 million consumers planned to shop on Super Saturday (the last Saturday before Christmas), according to a survey by the National Retail Federation and Prosper Insights & Analytics.
facts.quote: Nearly 142 million consumers plan to shop on the last Saturday before Christmas, according to the latest survey from the National Retail Federation and Prosper Insights & Analytics.

facts.fact: The number of expected Super Saturday shoppers was 126 million in 2017, when Super Saturday last fell on Dec. 23.
facts.quote: when 126 million consumers were expected to shop on that day in 2017.

facts.fact: About 53 million (37%) Super Saturday shoppers expected to shop exclusively in stores in 2023, up from about 44 million (28%) the prior year.
facts.quote: Approximately 53 million (37%) Super Saturday shoppers expect they will shop exclusively in stores this year, up from about 44 million (28%) last year

facts.fact: About 58 million (41%) Super Saturday shoppers planned to shop both online and in stores in 2023.
facts.quote: 58 million (41%) plan to shop both online and in stores.

facts.fact: About 31 million (22%) Super Saturday shoppers planned to shop exclusively online in 2023.
facts.quote: Around 31 million (22%) plan to shop exclusively online.

facts.fact: As of early December 2023, holiday shoppers had picked up about half (49%) of the items on their lists.
facts.quote: As of early December, holiday shoppers have picked up about half (49%) of the items on their lists.

facts.fact: Among consumers with more than half their shopping remaining, 36% said they were still figuring out what to buy.
facts.quote: For those who still have more than half of their shopping remaining, over one-third (36%) say they are still figuring out what to buy.

facts.fact: In November 2023, 85% of Thanksgiving weekend shoppers expected deals during the rest of the holiday season to be the same or better than Thanksgiving weekend.
facts.quote: In November, 85% of Thanksgiving weekend shoppers said they expected the deals during the rest of the holiday season to be the same or better than Thanksgiving weekend.

facts.fact: Online is the destination where 49% of consumers will finish their holiday shopping, according to the NRF survey.
facts.quote: Popular destinations where consumers will finish their shopping include online (49%), department stores (38%)

facts.fact: Department stores are a destination where 38% of consumers will finish their holiday shopping, according to the NRF survey.
facts.quote: department stores (38%), discount stores (28%)

facts.fact: Discount stores are a destination where 28% of consumers will finish their holiday shopping, according to the NRF survey.
facts.quote: discount stores (28%), clothing and accessories stores (26%)

facts.fact: Clothing and accessories stores are a destination where 26% of consumers will finish their holiday shopping, according to the NRF survey.
facts.quote: clothing and accessories stores (26%), and grocery stores (19%)

facts.fact: Grocery stores are a destination where 19% of consumers will finish their holiday shopping, according to the NRF survey.
facts.quote: and grocery stores (19%)

facts.fact: Toys were purchased as gifts by 34% of consumers so far, according to the NRF survey.
facts.quote: clothing (50%), toys (34%), gift cards (27%)

facts.fact: Gift cards were purchased as gifts by 27% of consumers so far, according to the NRF survey.
facts.quote: toys (34%), gift cards (27%), books and other media (24%)

facts.fact: Books and other media were purchased as gifts by 24% of consumers so far, according to the NRF survey.
facts.quote: gift cards (27%), books and other media (24%)

facts.fact: Personal care or beauty items were purchased as gifts by 23% of consumers so far, according to the NRF survey.
facts.quote: books and other media (24%), and personal care or beauty items (23%)

facts.fact: 70% of consumers say they plan to shop in the week following Dec. 25, according to the NRF survey.
facts.quote: Most consumers (70%) say they plan to shop in the week following Dec. 25.

facts.fact: 48% of consumers said they shop after Christmas to take advantage of holiday sales and promotions.
facts.quote: take advantage of holiday sales and promotions (48%), use gift cards (26%)

facts.fact: 26% of consumers said they shop after Christmas to use gift cards.
facts.quote: use gift cards (26%), and return or exchange unwanted gifts and holiday items (16%)

facts.fact: 16% of consumers said they shop after Christmas to return or exchange unwanted gifts and holiday items.
facts.quote: return or exchange unwanted gifts and holiday items (16%)

facts.fact: The NRF holiday survey asked 7,973 adult consumers about their holiday shopping plans.
facts.quote: The survey asked 7,973 adult consumers about their holiday shopping plans.

facts.fact: The survey was conducted Dec. 1-6 and has a margin of error of plus or minus 1.1 percentage points.
facts.quote: It was conducted Dec. 1-6 and has a margin of error of plus or minus 1.1 percentage points.

facts.fact: NRF expects holiday spending to grow between 3% and 4% over 2022, totaling $957.3 billion to $966.6 billion.
facts.quote: will grow between 3% and 4% over 2022, totaling $957.3 billion to $966.6 billion

facts.fact: NRF's forecast puts holiday sales in the range of $957.3 billion to $966.6 billion.
facts.quote: totaling $957.3 billion to $966.6 billion

facts.fact: Last year's holiday sales totaled $929.5 billion, according to NRF.
facts.quote: By comparison, last year holiday sales totaled $929.5 billion.

facts.fact: Retail contributes $3.9 trillion to annual GDP and supports one in four U.S. jobs, according to NRF.
facts.quote: contributing $3.9 trillion to annual GDP and supporting one in four U.S. jobs — 52 million working Americans.

facts.fact: Retail supports 52 million working Americans, according to NRF.
facts.quote: supporting one in four U.S. jobs — 52 million working Americans.
